officialTitle: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Limited-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer
setting: Consolidation after concurrent chemoradiotherapy in limited-stage SCLC

design.blinding: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; PFS by blinded independent central review
design.notes: Patients without progression after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy. Stratified by stage (I or II vs III) and receipt of PCI. First planned interim analysis of durvalumab vs placebo reported; durvalumab-tremelimumab arm remains blinded. 264 assigned to durvalumab, 200 to durvalumab-tremelimumab and 266 to placebo.

clinicalQuestion: Does consolidation durvalumab after concurrent chemoradiotherapy improve survival in limited-stage SCLC?

pico.population: Limited-stage SCLC without progression after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy (with or without PCI)
pico.intervention: Durvalumab every 4 weeks for up to 24 months
pico.outcomes: Dual primary: OS and PFS (BICR). Safety

arms.label: Durvalumab
arms.dosing: Durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks for up to 24 months
arms.doseSourceQuote: we assigned patients to receive durvalumab at a dose of 1500 mg, durvalumab (1500 mg) plus tremelimumab at a dose of 75 mg (four doses only), or placebo every 4 weeks for up to 24 months.

arms.label: Durvalumab + tremelimumab (results blinded)
arms.dosing: Durvalumab 1500 mg plus tremelimumab 75 mg (four doses only) every 4 weeks
arms.doseSourceQuote: we assigned patients to receive durvalumab at a dose of 1500 mg, durvalumab (1500 mg) plus tremelimumab at a dose of 75 mg (four doses only), or placebo every 4 weeks for up to 24 months.

publications.title: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Limited-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: First planned interim analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Durvalumab therapy led to significantly longer overall survival than placebo (median, 55.9 months [95% confidence interval {CI}, 37.3 to not reached] vs. 33.4 months [95% CI, 25.5 to 39.9]; hazard ratio for death, 0.73; 98.321% CI, 0.54 to 0.98; P = 0.01)

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS by blinded independent central review
outcomes.sourceQuote: as well as to significantly longer progression-free survival (median 16.6 months [95% CI, 10.2 to 28.2] vs. 9.2 months [95% CI, 7.4 to 12.9]; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.76; 97.195% CI, 0.59 to 0.98; P = 0.02).

safety.description: Adverse events with maximum grade 3 or 4
safety.sourceQuote: The incidence of adverse events with a maximum grade of 3 or 4 was 24.4% among patients receiving durvalumab and 24.2% among patients receiving placebo; adverse events led to discontinuation in 16.4% and 10.6% of the patients, respectively, and led to death in 2.7% and 1.9%.

safety.description: Grade 3 or 4 pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis
safety.sourceQuote: Pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis with a maximum grade of 3 or 4 occurred in 3.1% of the patients in the durvalumab group and in 2.6% of those in the placebo group.

strengths: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised phase III design with dual primary endpoints both met
PFS assessed by blinded independent central review
Stratified by stage and PCI use, reflecting real-world practice variation
limitations: Interim analysis; durvalumab-tremelimumab results remain blinded
Excluded patients who progressed after chemoradiotherapy, so applies only to those without progression

clinicalImplications.text: Consolidation durvalumab after concurrent chemoradiotherapy significantly prolonged OS and PFS in limited-stage SCLC, establishing the first immunotherapy consolidation standard in this setting, with a manageable pneumonitis rate.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Restage after chemoradiotherapy: patients without progression are candidates for consolidation durvalumab, with or without PCI.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 39268857. Alpha-adjusted CIs (98.321% for OS, 97.195% for PFS) as printed.
